entities.summary: Itō Mancio was a Japanese Jesuit who played a pivotal role in the first Japanese diplomatic mission to Europe, known as the Tenshō embassy. This embassy, which took place between 1587 and 1591, was a groundbreaking moment in the history of East Asian relations with the West. Itō Mancio was the head of the embassy and a Catholic priest, and his experiences during this time had a lasting impact on his life and the world. He died on November 13, 1612, at the age of 42. The Tenshō embassy was significant not only for its novelty but also for the cultural exchange it facilitated between Japan and Europe. Itō Mancio's legacy as a diplomat and a spiritual leader has endured, and his story continues to captivate historians and scholars today.
